LILT’s production team focuses on onboarding and localized content delivery for enterprise and mid-market customers, who use our AI technology for their multilingual content requirements.  Our team engages with customers from post-sales through steady-state production and is made up of experts in various functional and technical areas of LILT’s overall offering.  While we work in various locations, we are highly collaborative within the team and have tight interactions with our colleagues in the LILT Sales, Product, Engineering, and Operations teams.  Additionally, we operate as critical members of account-based teams that ensure LILT’s technology is utilized to deliver maximum value to our customers.  While we’re at it, we have fun and enjoy the ride together.




WHERE YOU’LL WORK

This is a contract position based out of India or Romania.



Authorization to work in India, Argentina, or Romania is a precondition of employment.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

We're looking for an experienced multimedia specialist with a localization background who loves solving hard problems, ensuring work is done on time to keep the customer experience seamless, and interacting with a variety of stakeholders. This position is for someone who has strong technical aptitude, extensive customer-facing experience, and the ability to manage competing priorities from multiple customers at once.



You will be responsible for scoping and processing multimedia content within our platform and partner platforms (e.g. CaptionHub, Articulate), ensuring accurate and timely completion of tasks.



You will work hand-in-hand with Sales, Production, Operations, and Engineering. You will be responsible for providing the technical expertise to make LILT customers successful.



You will have a broad range of skills and experience ranging from global multimedia content management lifecycle, a working knowledge of video and audio processing with respect to content pipelines and integrations. You will have the insight to make the connection between a customer’s specific business problems and LILT's solution, the customer-facing skills to communicate that connection and vision to a wide variety of technical and executive audiences, and the technical skills to be able to not only build demos and execute proof-of-concepts but also to provide consultative assistance on architecture and implementation.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Act as a localisation subject matter expert during the pre-sales cycle, providing guidance on e-learning content workflows, tools, and formats.
   

 - Scope and plan multimedia localisation projects for e-learning content across multiple languages, ensuring accuracy, efficiency, and scalability.
   

 - Prepare source e-learning files (e.g., Articulate Storyline, Rise, Captivate) for localisation, including extraction of translatable content, audio, and visual assets.
   

 - Reintegrate translated and localised materials, ensuring fully functional, linguistically accurate final e-learning modules.
   

 - Support customer onboarding and implementation, offering workflow guidance for e-learning localisation.
   

 - Manage localisation of video, voiceover, subtitling, and interactive learning assets in line with project requirements.
   

 - Provide best practices for managing localisation-ready content and advise on automation opportunities in e-learning localisation workflows.
   

 - Operate and maintain localisation tools and platforms, supporting both AI-driven and human-led localisation processes.
   

 - Review localised e-learning content, including SCORM packages, for quality, technical accuracy, and adherence to brand and platform standards.
   

 - Perform final QA checks ("final eyes") and prepare final files for delivery to clients or internal stakeholders.
   

 - Act as the go-to expert on e-learning localisation workflows and tools across the organisation.
   

 - Meet SLAs and KPIs for engineering and localisation delivery.
   


SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

 - 3+ years of experience in e-learning localisation or multimedia localisation with a strong focus on learning and development content.
   

 - Deep expertise in preparing and localising content developed in Articulate Storyline, Rise, Adobe Captivate, and similar authoring tools.
   

 - Strong understanding of SCORM/xAPI compliance, LMS integrations, and common e-learning file types.
   

 - Proficiency in video subtitling, editing, and localisation, including experience with voiceover, dubbing, audio integration, and subtitle syncing.
   

 - Experience with video editing software (e.g., Adobe Premiere Pro, Camtasia, Audacity) and managing media files at scale.
   

 - Familiarity with multimedia file formats and localisation-friendly formats (e.g., XLIFF, JSON, XML, STRINGS, SRT, VTT).
   

 - Exposure to CAT tools and localisation platforms (TMX editors, translation memory tools, OCR, and alignment software).
   

 - Solid understanding of character encoding, formatting rules, and localisation QA standards.
   

 - Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
   

 - Comfortable managing large file repositories and understanding of file transfer methods (FTP, SFTP, cloud-based systems).

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY 

We are seeking detail-oriented human reviewers with a strong understanding of their local cultural context to support a range of AI training and evaluation projects.

In this role, you will work across diverse task types, including evaluating prompts and AI-generated outputs, reviewing and correcting text, analyzing multimedia content, contributing voice recordings, among others.

You will contribute to ensuring high-quality results by applying careful judgment to factors such as accuracy, clarity, cultural appropriateness, brand alignment, and overall effectiveness in meeting task objectives. This work requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and nuanced judgment informed by real-world standards, local norms, and market expectations.




WHAT YOU’LL DELIVER 

 - Depending on the task, you may be asked to generate original content or assess AI-generated outputs.

 - Deliver culturally relevant and appropriate content by applying local insight into tone, symbolism, visual cues, and market fit.

 - Spot common issues such as visual artefacts, inconsistent style, translation errors, or cultural mismatches.

 - Provide concise, structured annotations that can be used directly for model improvement.

 - Apply evaluation guidelines consistently and participate in calibration and QA processes to ensure aligned scoring and judgment standards




QUALIFICATIONS 

 - Native fluency in the target language

 - Strong command of English

 - Experience as AI reviewer, annotator, or evaluator preferred

 - Comfortable working with both textual and audio/video materials

 - Ability to follow detailed guidelines consistently and provide clear feedback

 - High attention to detail and ability to thoroughly and accurately categorize content

As a Subject Matter Expert, you will create and review realistic, high-quality scenarios that reflect operational, administrative, compliance, public safety, social service, and community engagement challenges across government institutions. Your expertise will help ensure AI systems understand and respond accurately within highly regulated and citizen-focused environments.




WHAT YOU’LL DELIVER

 - Design realistic government scenarios in Hindi or English grounded in Indian public sector contexts (e.g., administrative operations, social services, compliance reviews, public safety coordination, community programs, citizen service delivery)

 - Adapt structured evaluation rubrics for operational problem-solving, policy interpretation, case management, and decision-making tasks

 - Review AI and human-generated responses for factual accuracy, procedural compliance, cultural appropriateness, and operational realism

 - Contribute to “gold standard” solutions reflecting public sector and government best practices


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Native Hindi with strong professional English proficiency

 - 5+ years of professional experience in government, public administration, social services, public safety, compliance, or community programs

 - Background in one or more relevant roles: Administrative Services Management, Child/Family/School Social Work, Compliance & Regulatory Affairs, Police or Public Safety Supervision, Recreation & Community Services, or related government functions

 - Strong understanding of public sector workflows, operational procedures, regulatory requirements, and Indian government environments

 - Grow without limits. As a Lilt contractor you get access to diverse, innovative projects that expand your portfolio and sharpen your skills across industries and domains.

Role summary

The IT Support Specialist (Network, Office Buildout & Physical Security) is the hands-on, on-site IT presence for Ontic’s Pune office - focused on planning, deploying, and supporting network infrastructure, office technology, and physical security coordination to enable a smooth office launch and ongoing operations. This role partners closely with IT, Information Sec Security, DevOps, Facilities, Legal, and local vendors to execute installs, troubleshoot issues, maintain a reliable and secure office environment, and keep required physical security controls organized, documented, and audit-ready.



Schedule & location

 - On-site: Monday - Friday, 10:00am–7:00pm (may vary once the office is opened and user behaviors require a different support window)

 - Location: Ontic - Pune, India (on-site office presence required)

 - Attendance: Able to reliably commute and be in the office every workday; comfortable supporting occasional after-hours cutovers during office setup or network changes


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


OFFICE IT LAUNCH & ONGOING BUILDOUT OPERATIONS (PUNE)

 - Execute IT workstreams for the active office opening and startup phase: ongoing network optimization, equipment staging, and day-to-day IT support

 - Maintain and refine the office IT operational checklist (network gear, spares inventory, labeling standards, architecture diagrams, and handover documentation)


ENDPOINT & ON-SITE SUPPORT

 - Provide on-site and remote end-user support and incident triage for Pune teammates (macOS/Windows), prioritizing issues that impact office productivity

 - Own tickets from intake to resolution; provide clear updates, timelines, and documentation

 - Support day-to-day endpoint administration and lifecycle needs (enrollment, compliance posture, patching, refreshes, repairs, offboarding)

 - Administer and troubleshoot endpoint management tooling, including:
   
   - Jamf (macOS management)
   
   - Microsoft Intune (Windows + mobile management where applicable)
   
   - Jamf Security Cloud (where applicable)

 - Support Android devices (deployment, troubleshooting, basic management workflows) and Linux endpoints where needed (diagnostics, package/tooling basics, SSH, logs)

 - Work with identity/access concepts and basic administration tasks as needed (SSO, MFA, conditional access concepts, basic Active Directory users/groups/permissions troubleshooting in partnership with centralized IT)

 - Provide support for office printers and peripherals as needed


NETWORKING, NETWORK EQUIPMENT & ARCHITECTURE

 - Deploy, configure, and support core office networking components, including:
   
   - Switches, routers, firewalls/security appliances, and wireless access points
   
   - Network closets/racks, patch panels, cable management, labeling, and inventory

 - Own day-to-day troubleshooting for network issues (wired/wireless): DHCP/DNS, VLANs, routing, NAT, Wi‑Fi performance, authentication/captive portals, and connectivity to SaaS/VPN resources

 - Implement and maintain network segmentation and access controls in partnership with IT/InfoSec (guest vs corp networks, IoT/AV networks, least privilege)

 - Document network architecture: logical diagrams, IP plans, VLAN maps, SSIDs, port assignments, circuit details, and standard configurations

 - Participate in network change planning: maintenance windows, rollout plans, validation steps, and rollback procedures


PHYSICAL SECURITY COORDINATION & COMPLIANCE

 - Serve as the local execution owner for Pune physical security readiness and vendor oversight, coordinating access control, CCTV, visitor management, and ensuring vendors meet required standards and documentation expectations.

 - Administer the office Genetec security system.

 - Help maintain required site documentation, including building agreements, emergency response plans, site risk assessments, evacuation information, and safety evidence

 - Verify and document required safety and security controls such as fire extinguisher placement, inspection status, posted evacuation routes, and physical access procedures

 - Organize and maintain physical security evidence for audits, compliance reviews, and ongoing control validation

 - Support ongoing reviews of site access, visitor procedures, security coverage, and office technology risks

 - Identify and escalate gaps that could create operational, compliance, safety, or security risk


SECURITY TOOLING & ENDPOINT PROTECTION (DAY-TO-DAY)

 - Support day-to-day administration, deployment, health checks, and basic troubleshooting for endpoint security tooling (CrowdStrike, Rapid7, Jamf, etc.)

 - Follow Ontic security policies and IT standards; help enforce them with a customer-first mindset (least privilege, MFA, device compliance, patching, phishing awareness, secure configuration)


A/V AND CONFERENCE ROOM SUPPORT

 - Support meeting room readiness (displays, microphones/speakers, conferencing devices) and basic troubleshooting

 - Coordinate installations and upgrades for conference room equipment with vendors where applicable


INVENTORY & ASSET COORDINATION

 - Maintain accurate inventory for Pune office IT/network assets (network gear, spares, adapters, peripherals)

 - Coordinate receiving, staging, and shipping/returns of equipment in partnership with centralized IT


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years of hands-on IT support experience with a strong emphasis on networking plus strong endpoint support fundamentals

 - Experience deploying and supporting network equipment in an office environment (switching, wireless, firewall/security edge)

 - Ability to read/create network diagrams and maintain accurate documentation (IP plans, VLAN maps, rack layouts)

 - Proven experience executing IT work for office buildouts, expansions, or relocations (vendor coordination, installs, cutovers, validation)

 - Experience coordinating office physical security activities, vendor workstreams, or site readiness requirements

 - Ability to maintain compliance-oriented documentation and evidence for office controls, safety procedures, and audit requests

 - Solid troubleshooting skills with a structured approach (hypothesis-driven triage, packet/path reasoning, clear incident notes)

 - Strong communication skills and customer-first mindset; able to coordinate across time zones with remote teams

 - Comfort working with ticketing systems and maintaining operational discipline (updates, timelines, documentation)

 - Strong working knowledge of macOS and Windows troubleshooting and support in a business environment

 - Familiarity with MDM/endpoint management concepts (enrollment, configuration profiles/policies, compliance, patching, lifecycle)


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

CORE BEHAVIORS

 - Calm under pressure during outages and cutovers; prioritizes safety, security, and clear communication

 - Collaborative and reliable follows through and closes loops

Job Summary

OpenGov’s Professional Services (PS) team delivers configurable, scalable solutions to state and local governments using Government App Builder (GAB) — OpenGov’s proprietary low-code/no-code application development platform.

As a Business Application Developer III, you will design, configure, and enhance customer or business specific applications using platform capabilities, configuration, data modeling, workflow automation, and limited scripting.

You will split your time between:

 - Designing and configuring business applications using Government App Builder

 - Partnering directly with implementation teams and customers to translate business processes into scalable, automated solutions

 

This role is ideal for a technically strong problem solver who understands data modeling, workflow logic, and business process design — but does not require heavy full-stack engineering in frameworks such as React, NodeJS, or Java. You will play a key role in delivering high-impact solutions that modernize government operations.

 

Key Responsibilities

 - Design structured data models including entity relationships and cross-table references.

 - Implement task assignments, notification rules, and automation components.

 - Translate documented decision trees and business rules into platform logic.

 - Ensure scalability of workflows across departments and user roles.

 4. Business Rule Implementation & Light Scripting

 - Implement conditional logic using platform configuration tools.

 1. Write limited JavaScript (or similar scripting) for:

 - Complex validations

 - Conditional routing

 - Data transformation logic

 - Maintain clean, reusable logic patterns without overengineering or heavy custom code.

 5. Integrations & Interoperability

 - Configure and validate integrations between Government App Builder and external systems (e.g., ERP, financial systems).

 - Ensure timely delivery of configured applications within broader project timelines.

 - Maintain high standards of quality, documentation, and responsiveness.

Job Summary

The Senior Manager, HR Technology owns the strategy, roadmap, administration, and continuous improvement of OpenGov’s HR technology stack, ensuring the systems and integrations that manage employee data across the employee lifecycle are reliable, compliant, scalable, and aligned to the needs of a global workforce. Based in Pune, India and reporting to the Director of Enterprise Applications and Engineering, this role sets direction for HR technology across the organization and leads a team that includes HR application administrators and a staff-level HR Systems Architect. It partners with stakeholders across the US and India — HR Operations, Payroll, Benefits, Talent Acquisition, Talent Management, HR Business Partners, IT, and Workplace — to maintain, modernize, and streamline the systems that support the full employee lifecycle, from hire to retire and onboarding to offboarding.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned HR technology leader who pairs strategic ownership with deep, hands-on expertise — comfortable setting the HR technology roadmap and standards while staying close enough to the Workday stack and broader application portfolio to guide technical decisions, unblock the team, and ensure quality. This person leads and develops the team, including a staff-level architect and senior individual contributors, and brings domain depth spanning both US and India geographies, ideally complemented by experience with NetSuite or a comparable ERP. The Senior Manager owns the technical relationship with Ashby (ATS), oversees the employee engagement survey platform, owns HR data governance in partnership with IT, and guides integration/systems architecture across the HR ecosystem — including how HRIS data flows into NetSuite/ERP and downstream platforms.

Responsibilities

Leadership, Strategy & People Management

 - Own the HR technology strategy and multi-year roadmap, aligning system investments and priorities with HR and business objectives and communicating direction to stakeholders and leadership.

JOB SUMMARY:

The Staff HR Technology Architect is the senior technical authority for OpenGov’s HR technology ecosystem, responsible for the architecture, integration design, and long-term technical direction of the systems that manage employee data across the entire employee lifecycle. Based in Pune and reporting to the Director of Enterprise Applications and Engineering, this individual-contributor role sets the technical vision for the Workday platform and the broader HR application portfolio, ensuring the ecosystem is scalable, secure, compliant, and aligned to the needs of a global workforce across the US and India.

We are looking for a seasoned architect with deep domain and technical expertise across the Workday platform and the adjacent, integrated systems that make up the HR technology ecosystem — spanning payroll, benefits, talent management, talent acquisition, onboarding and offboarding, employee engagement, compliance, and HR operations. This is a hands-on, staff-level individual contributor with a dotted-line leadership mandate: no direct reports, but expected to guide and mentor HR application administrators, lead virtual teams on major initiatives, and influence the direction both technical and business teams take with HR technology. While the role is primarily architecture and design, it also carries hands-on technical delivery — the architect personally builds and delivers the most complex or high-risk integrations, configurations, and reports. The architect owns integration architecture and the HR data model end to end across best-of-breed systems, partners with the Manager, HR Technology on delivery, and serves as the design authority on data governance, security, and emerging AI and automation across the stack.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

Technical Architecture & Systems Design

 - Own the end-to-end architecture of the HR technology ecosystem — Workday (Core HCM, Payroll, Benefits, Absence, Time Tracking, Compensation, Recruiting, Talent, Reporting, and Security) and the surrounding application portfolio — establishing design standards, patterns, and technical roadmaps.

 - Own the architecture across a best-of-breed, multi-platform landscape — the core HRIS (Workday) plus payroll (e.g., ADP), applicant tracking (Ashby), employee engagement (CultureAmp), ERP (e.g., NetSuite), SSO/identity, compliance/training platforms, data-warehousing and BI tooling (e.g., Snowflake), and iPaaS/integration platforms (e.g., Workato) — ensuring the systems interoperate as a coherent whole.

 - Define target-state architecture and multi-year technical roadmaps that scale with a growing, globally distributed workforce, balancing configuration, extensibility, and total cost of ownership.

 - Evaluate new Workday releases, features, and third-party solutions; make build-vs-configure-vs-buy recommendations and lead architecture and design reviews.

 - Provide deep, hands-on technical expertise across the ecosystem — anchored in the Workday stack (advanced configuration, the business process framework, calculated fields, security design, and complex reporting) and extending to adjacent platforms such as ADP, Ashby, CultureAmp, and NetSuite/ERP.

Integration Architecture & Data Flows

 - Design and govern the integration architecture across the HR ecosystem (e.g., ADP, Ashby, engagement survey, SSO/identity, ERP, and downstream data-warehouse/BI platforms such as Snowflake), leveraging iPaaS/integration platforms (e.g., Workato) where appropriate and establishing patterns, standards, and error handling and monitoring.

 - Own the HR data model and the flow of employee data from hire to retire, ensuring integrity, lineage, and consistency across integrated systems.

 - Serve as design authority for Workday integrations (EIB, Core Connectors, Studio, and web service APIs), iPaaS platforms (e.g., Workato), and downstream data platform feeds.

 - Maintain a working understanding of how HRIS data ties into ERP (e.g., NetSuite) and other enterprise systems, and lead the design of those interfaces.

Technical Strategy & Influence

 - Set the technical direction for HR technology and influence the decisions both technical and business teams make when adopting or changing technology.

 - Partner with HR Operations, Payroll, Benefits, Talent Acquisition, Talent Management, HR Business Partners, IT, and Workplace leaders to translate business strategy into a coherent systems strategy.

 - Act as a trusted technical advisor to leadership, framing trade-offs, risks, and options for major HR technology investments and platform decisions.

 - Provide dotted-line technical leadership and mentorship to HR application administrators; lead virtual and matrixed teams on large initiatives and build technical depth and backup coverage across critical domains.

Data Governance, Security & AI

 - Serve as the design authority for HR data governance, privacy, and security — defining data structures, access models, and controls across the US and India.

 - Establish standards for HR data quality, master data, and reporting and analytics that feed data-warehouse and BI platforms (e.g., Snowflake).

 - Identify and pilot opportunities to apply automation and AI within the HR technology stack, establishing responsible-use and data-handling guardrails.

 - Ensure the architecture supports compliance requirements across geographies (audits, policy acknowledgements, and mandatory training) and evolving data-privacy regulations.

Delivery, Vendors & Best Practices

 - Lead complex, cross-functional HR technology projects end to end from an architecture and design standpoint — shaping solutions, reviewing designs, and guiding delivery teams.

 - Stay hands-on with technical delivery — personally building and delivering the most complex or high-risk configurations, integrations, and reports rather than limiting the role to design and oversight.

 - Partner with the Manager, HR Technology and the administration team to translate architecture into configuration, and maintain documentation of architecture, standards, and system specifications.

 - Manage strategic third-party vendor and implementation-partner relationships from a technical and architecture perspective.

 - Stay current on Workday releases, HR technology trends, and best practices; exhibit sound judgment, discretion, and confidentiality in handling sensitive employee data.




REQUIREMENTS AND PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:

 - Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required.

 - 10+ years of progressive HR technology / HRIS functional and technical experience, including significant time in an architecture, principal, or senior technical individual-contributor capacity.

 - Demonstrated experience as a technical authority who sets direction and influences both technical and business stakeholders — this is a senior individual-contributor role, not an entry-level or first architecture role.

 - Deep, hands-on expertise in a core HRIS — Workday strongly preferred — across the full module stack (Absence, Benefits, Compensation, Core HCM, Payroll, Recruiting, Reporting, Security, Talent, Time Tracking), including advanced configuration and the business process framework.

 - Hands-on experience across a multi-platform HR technology ecosystem — not limited to a single HRIS — including payroll (e.g., ADP), applicant tracking (Ashby preferred), employee engagement (CultureAmp preferred), SSO/identity, and compliance/training platforms.

 - Strong Workday integration expertise (EIB, Core Connectors, Studio, and web services/APIs) and proven experience designing enterprise integration architectures, including iPaaS/integration platforms (e.g., Workato).

 - Expertise in HR data modeling, data governance, and how HRIS data flows into downstream data-warehouse and BI systems (e.g., Snowflake).

 - Experience with data-warehousing tools (e.g., Snowflake) and iPaaS/integration platforms (e.g., Workato).

 - Willingness and ability to perform hands-on technical delivery — configuration, integration development, and reporting — in addition to architecture, design, and oversight; this is not a design-only role.

 - Broad domain expertise across payroll, benefits, talent management, talent acquisition, onboarding/offboarding, employee engagement, and general HR operations.

 - Experience supporting HR systems across multiple geographies, ideally including both the US and India.

 - Proficiency with Workday report writing and complex calculated fields.

 - Experience with an applicant tracking system (Ashby preferred) and an employee engagement survey platform (CultureAmp preferred).

 - Demonstrated ability to mentor administrators and provide dotted-line technical leadership without formal reporting authority.

 - Strong understanding of HR compliance, data privacy, and security considerations across regions.

 - Exposure to automation and AI applications within HR technology a plus.

 - Familiarity with NetSuite or a comparable ERP, and how HRIS data integrates with it, a plus (nice to have).

 - Excellent communication skills, able to influence and align technical and business stakeholders at all levels of a globally distributed organization.

 - Workday certifications (e.g., Integrations, HCM, or Pro) preferred.

 - Experience using Google Workspace a plus.

 - Exhibits sound judgment, discretion, and confidentiality.

The Implementation Engineer III is a senior technical delivery leader who partners with government customers to bring OpenGov cloud software to life, owning the most complex product configurations and the underlying data migrations across a portfolio of implementations. This role leads requirements validation, configuration and data reviews, platform configuration and testing, data migration and reconciliation, and user enablement, guiding customers through the full deployment journey from kickoff to go-live while setting the technical quality bar for the team.

Acting as a trusted advisor with deep product knowledge and advanced data and database expertise, the Implementation Engineer III understands each customer's goals, pain points, and workflows, and translates them into scalable, maintainable solutions. This role blends hands-on technical delivery, including data transformation and migration (ETL), and scripting, with a consultative, customer-first approach. It also mentors less-experienced engineers, reviews their configuration and data work, and drives the process and quality improvements that raise the standard of implementation delivery across the organization.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Lead the data migration, configuration, and testing of OpenGov cloud software for the most complex government implementations across the United States

 - Perform configuration reviews across the team, validating that platform setup aligns with documented requirements, product best practices, and long-term maintainability before go-live

 - Perform data reviews, validating migrated data for completeness, accuracy, and integrity, and reconciling source-to-target data so the product reflects trusted, audit-ready customer data

 - Own complex customer data migration end to end, including database schema mapping, ETL tool configuration, and advanced scripting, to ensure the product is populated with accurate, validated data

 - Confirm and pressure-test customer requirements across both configuration and data, resolving ambiguity and advising customers on the optimal solution design

 - Design and execute comprehensive test scenarios that validate the configuration and migrated data produce accurate, expected outcomes prior to go-live

 - Serve as the primary technical point of contact for government / customer stakeholder like Budget Directors, IT personnel, and decision-makers, guiding them through the deployment and integration process

 - Identify recurring customer pain points and partner with cross-functional teams to simplify, enhance, and automate processes that improve customer workflows and delivery efficiency

 - Mentor and coach Associate and mid-level Implementation Engineers, reviewing their configuration and data work and helping accelerate their technical growth

 - Define and improve implementation standards, templates, playbooks, and reusable tooling that increase the quality, consistency, and speed of delivery

 - Partner closely with the Project Management, Customer Success Management, Data/Integration, and Product teams to ensure a consistent customer experience, and channel field feedback into the product roadmap
   
   


REQUIREMENTS AND PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

 - 6 to 9 years of experience in software implementation, data migration, or technical consulting, ideally with enterprise or SaaS products

 - 5+ years of hands-on SQL scripting experience, including complex queries, data transformation, and reconciliation

 - 3+ years of Python, or similar, scripting experience for automation and data processing

 - Deep experience with database technologies and with ETL and data-migration concepts and tools, including schema design and performance considerations

 - Experience implementing AI-driven solutions for automation, workflow optimization, and data-driven insights, leveraging modern frameworks and AI models

 - Demonstrated ability to deliver complex implementations end to end and to mentor or provide technical guidance to less-experienced engineers

 - Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with a strong teamwork and customer-service mentality across executive and technical stakeholders

 - Strong attention to detail, with the proven ability to validate, reconcile, and sign off on data and configuration for accuracy

 - Ability to adapt to a rapidly changing product and respond strategically to evolving customer needs

 - Bachelor's degree in a technical, or related field

You will oversee the strategy and execution of application security initiatives, embedding industry-leading standards such as OWASP into our development lifecycle. The ideal candidate is collaborative, approachable, and an excellent communicator, capable of building trust with engineers, product leaders, and executives alike.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Lead and mentor the Application Security team to drive engagement, growth, and technical excellence.

 - Build and execute the organization’s application security roadmap to strengthen the security posture of all product suites and APIs.

 - Champion secure development practices by embedding OWASP ASVS and OWASP Top 10 guidance into coding standards, architecture reviews, and threat modeling.

 - Oversee the selection, deployment, and integration of AppSec tools (e.g., SAST, DAST, SCA, ASPM) into CI/CD pipelines.

 - Partner with Engineering, DevOps, and Product to ensure secure coding, design reviews, and vulnerability management processes are followed.

 - Report on risk metrics, remediation progress, and program effectiveness to senior leadership and stakeholders.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 7+ years of combined experience in Application Security, Software Engineering, or related fields; 3+ years leading or managing security teams.

ABOUT THE ROLE

OpenGov is hiring a Product Engineer to own a domain inside our ERP — the financial system of record for state and local government. You will own a product area end to end: customer discovery, the roadmap, the user experience, the build, the launch, and the adoption number. This is a new kind of role, born from AI's ability to handle execution work that once required three specialists. What AI cannot do is decide what matters, sit with a finance director through a budget cycle, make the right call in an ambiguous compliance question, or own whether a product succeeds. That is what Product Engineers do.

 

The shift to Product Engineering is primarily about owning the product — not becoming an engineer. The best Product Engineers are obsessed with the who and the why: who are these customers, what do they actually need, and what business outcomes depend on solving their problems. The how — writing code, building interfaces — is a skill you grow into using AI-native tooling. It is a career accelerator, not a job requirement on day one.

 

"Product Engineer" is two words — but the first word is the one that matters most. The second is how you get there.

 

We are hiring for judgment. You will own a domain where the decisions are load-bearing: a chart-of-accounts choice that a county lives with for a decade, a reporting model that either satisfies an auditor or does not. We expect you to make those calls, write down why, and defend them when the facts change.

 


THE DOMAIN

ERP at OpenGov is a suite, and this role owns a domain within it. Depending on fit, that domain sits in or across:

 - Financial Management — general ledger and the chart of accounts, accounts payable, accounts receivable and cash receipts, fixed assets, purchase card, requisitions, bank reconciliation, project accounting.

 - Budgeting & Performance — budget creation and proposals on the ERP chart of accounts, worksheets, multi-period adoption, amendments and transfers, workforce planning, performance measures.

 - Reporting & Financial Statements — the financial report engine, multi-hierarchy and multi-entity reporting, GASB-compliant statements, the datasets and pipelines beneath them, and the transparency surfaces governments publish to residents.

 - Procurement — intake through solicitation, evaluation, award, and contract management, and the vendor record that connects procurement to AP.

 

Adjacent domains — payroll and HCM, utility billing, tax and revenue, permitting, asset management — sit alongside yours in the same platform. You will not own them, but your decisions will touch them, and you are expected to coordinate rather than escalate.

 

The hard, specific problems in this domain right now include chart-of-accounts migration and mutation, multi-entity and blended component-unit structures (a county and its school district, a city and its authorities), reporting parity for customers moving off a legacy product, and audit-readiness as a product capability rather than a services engagement. If those problems sound interesting rather than tedious, this is the right role for you.

 


WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - A domain. A defined set of customers, problems, and measurable business outcomes you are accountable for driving. You are the DRI — the directly responsible individual — for all things product in that domain.

 - The roadmap. What gets built, in what order, and why, informed by customer research, competitive context, and business goals. You set it, defend it publicly, and update it when facts change. Aha and the Roadmap Portal stay the source of truth so GTM can work from it.

 - The end-to-end user experience. From first interaction to last, you define the flow and validate the design within the design system — not just the requirements.

 - The ship. From idea to live in customers' hands. You drive intent, design, build coordination, launch, and iteration without handing off across three roles. Engineers review your PRs the way they review each other's.

 - The number. Adoption, go-live and retention targets, and the revenue tied to your domain. The outcome belongs to you.

 - Field time. Product Engineers are members of Customer Product Squads alongside an Engagement Lead and a Solution Architect, and stay on accounts after go-live. Expect roughly 20–25 hours per implementation — concentrated in discovery, with lighter oversight through configuration and training — capped at about a quarter of your time. The other three quarters is your domain. When a bug surfaces on site, you fix it on site rather than filing a ticket and waiting.

 


HOW AI WORKS IN THIS ROLE

AI-native tooling handles a significant portion of what product managers and UX designers historically spent their time on. That time is yours to redirect toward higher-leverage work.

 - Spec writing. The prototype is the spec. You build first, in the product repo, with AI skills that carry our standards; the product brief is generated from what you built. Nobody writes a PRD first.

 - UX design. AI generates screens from the design system based on your flow definitions, and design-review agents sanity-check what you built. You make the product decisions within the system and escalate genuinely new patterns.

 - Research synthesis. AI clusters and themes interview notes, call transcripts, support cases, and product usage. You interpret what it means for the roadmap and make the call.

 - Release content. AI drafts release notes, in-app announcements, demo data, and enablement material from what you shipped.

 - Code review and test coverage. Automated review catches style, security, and regression issues; AI generates test cases from your acceptance criteria. You stay accountable for quality outcomes, and your acceptance criteria have to be precise enough to verify.

 - Competitive and regulatory monitoring. AI surfaces competitor moves and changes in accounting standards and state reporting requirements. You form the point of view and decide what it means for the roadmap.

 

What AI does not do: understand your customers, make the call on what matters, own the outcome, or build the cross-functional trust that makes things ship. That is the job.

You are also expected to improve the tooling itself — identify gaps in AI harnesses, skills, and design system coverage, and surface them as platform investment requests with a clear business case.

 

Key Responsibilities

 - Define and communicate the product vision for your domain, grounded in customer research, competitive context, and business goals — not inherited from committee.

 - Conduct and synthesize discovery with government finance staff: translate what you hear into clear, defensible decisions about what to build and what to cut.

 - Own the roadmap: prioritize ruthlessly, explain your reasoning publicly, and revise it when new facts warrant it.

 - Define user experience flows and interaction patterns within the design system; escalate to platform and design when a genuinely new system-level pattern is required.

 - Build. Use AI-native tooling to move from intent to working software in the product repo, validate with customers, and iterate. Own your PRs through review.

 - Write acceptance criteria precise enough for automated tests to verify, and treat quality as a pipeline property rather than a hardening phase.

 - Partner with engineering leads and squad engineers to unblock builds and resolve ambiguity in real time without becoming a bottleneck.

 - Embed with Professional Services on implementations and migrations: run discovery, close the gap between what the product does and what the customer configured, and feed what you learn straight back into the roadmap.

 - Track adoption, usage, go-live health, and business outcomes; use them to drive the next iteration, not just to report status.

 - Represent your domain in customer conversations, QBRs, steering committees, and cross-functional reviews — the full commercial picture, not just the feature set.

 - Coordinate directly with adjacent domains when a customer need spans more than one, and bring a recommendation rather than a question.

 

Core Skill Sets — Non-Negotiables

Ranked in order of importance and impact. The first three are the screen; the rest are the bar.

 - Ownership under ambiguity. You make good decisions with incomplete information and iterate faster than you wait for certainty. One DRI means there is nobody else to point to, and that energizes you rather than worrying you. Candidates who have only operated inside a PM-designer-engineer trio, with someone else accountable for the outcome, will struggle here.

 - Demonstrated product ownership with a track record. Product management, product design, or a closely adjacent role, where you shipped things customers actually use and can point precisely to what you owned versus what the team owned. This is an individual-contributor role, not a management one.

 - Depth in a complex, workflow-heavy, compliance-bound B2B domain. Financial software, ERP, accounting, or a comparably regulated enterprise domain. The general requirement is that you have owned a product where being wrong had consequences beyond a churned subscription.

 - Customer discovery you have actually run. You have conducted discovery, synthesized the research yourself, and changed a roadmap or a design because of what you learned — with a specific example.

 - Written communication. You can articulate a product decision clearly enough that engineering, design, services, and leadership all walk away aligned, without a follow-up meeting. Expect a writing signal in the process.

 - Willingness to build. You do not need to arrive as a developer, but code fluency has to read to you as a career accelerator rather than a threat. Experience in AI-native workflows is a plus; willingness to become proficient in them is required.

 


PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

 - Government finance, public sector accounting, or GovTech SaaS — or direct experience as a finance officer, budget analyst, auditor, or controller.

 - Familiarity with fund accounting, chart-of-accounts design, GASB reporting, the annual budget cycle, or external audit workflows.

 - Experience with data migration or platform replacement programs, where the hard part was the customer's existing data rather than the new feature.

 - Multi-entity or multi-organization data models, consolidated reporting, or component-unit structures.

 - Hands-on time with AI development tooling — Claude Code, Cursor, or similar — and with design systems and component libraries.

At OpenGov, finding the right people to drive revenue and deliver for our customers starts with a great sourcing engine. As a Recruiter / Sr. Recruiter, you’ll be the first point of contact for candidates pursuing roles in India — building pipelines, sparking conversations, and qualifying talent before passing it to the recruiting team. Based in Pune on a 6-month contract, you’ll partner closely with our TAs to keep hiring moving fast, especially during high-volume hiring drives where interview coordination becomes just as critical as the outreach itself. If you’re energized by the hunt, love a great candidate conversation, and take pride in keeping things organized and on-time, this role is for you.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Source candidates proactively using LinkedIn Recruiter, job boards, and creative outbound tactics — identifying both active and passive talent that matches the profile for each requisition.

 - Maintain a healthy, organized pipeline on Ashby, keeping candidate records, outreach status, and screen notes updated so the recruiting team always has a clear view of where candidates stand.

 - Coordinate interview scheduling during hiring drives — managing candidate and interviewer calendars, sending confirmations, and ensuring a smooth, on-time interview experience for all parties.

 - Draft and send personalized outreach messages to passive candidates that reflect OpenGov’s mission and the opportunity at hand, balancing volume with authenticity to maximize response rates.

 - Collaborate daily with the Recruiter, sharing pipeline updates, flagging blockers, and aligning on sourcing priorities as requisition needs shift.

 - Serve as a positive brand ambassador in every candidate interaction, ensuring that even candidates who aren’t a fit walk away with a strong impression of OpenGov.

 - Comfortable using AI-native tools to accelerate workflows and improve efficiency.

 - Proficiency with LinkedIn Recruiter and at least one ATS platform for pipeline tracking and candidate management

 - Strong written communication skills — able to craft outreach that gets responses and represents the brand well

 - Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage candidate pipelines and interview schedules simultaneously without dropping the ball

 - Comfortable using AI-native tools to accelerate workflows and improve efficiency



Preferred Experience:

 - Experience sourcing GTM talent specifically in the Indian market, with familiarity with the Pune talent landscape and local compensation norms

 - Prior experience with Ashby or a similar ATS

 - Background in high-volume or hiring-drive environments where speed and coordination are equally important

 - Familiarity with GovTech, enterprise SaaS, or public sector software — helpful context for qualifying candidates on role and mission fit

JOB SUMMARY

The Implementation Engineer III is a senior technical delivery leader who partners with government customers to bring OpenGov cloud software to life, owning the most complex product configurations and the underlying data migrations across a portfolio of implementations. This role leads requirements validation, configuration and data reviews, platform configuration and testing, data migration and reconciliation, and user enablement, guiding customers through the full deployment journey from kickoff to go-live while setting the technical quality bar for the team.

Acting as a trusted advisor with deep product knowledge and advanced data and database expertise, the Implementation Engineer III understands each customer's goals, pain points, and workflows, and translates them into scalable, maintainable solutions. This role blends hands-on technical delivery, including data transformation and migration (ETL), and scripting, with a consultative, customer-first approach. It also mentors less-experienced engineers, reviews their configuration and data work, and drives the process and quality improvements that raise the standard of implementation delivery across the organization.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Lead the data migration, configuration, and testing of OpenGov cloud software for the most complex government implementations across the United States

 - Perform configuration reviews across the team, validating that platform setup aligns with documented requirements, product best practices, and long-term maintainability before go-live

 - Perform data reviews, validating migrated data for completeness, accuracy, and integrity, and reconciling source-to-target data so the product reflects trusted, audit-ready customer data

 - Own complex customer data migration end to end, including database schema mapping, ETL tool configuration, and advanced scripting, to ensure the product is populated with accurate, validated data

 - Confirm and pressure-test customer requirements across both configuration and data, resolving ambiguity and advising customers on the optimal solution design

 - Design and execute comprehensive test scenarios that validate the configuration and migrated data produce accurate, expected outcomes prior to go-live

 - Serve as the primary technical point of contact for government / customer stakeholder like Budget Directors, IT personnel, and decision-makers, guiding them through the deployment and integration process

 - Identify recurring customer pain points and partner with cross-functional teams to simplify, enhance, and automate processes that improve customer workflows and delivery efficiency

 - Mentor and coach Associate and mid-level Implementation Engineers, reviewing their configuration and data work and helping accelerate their technical growth

 - Define and improve implementation standards, templates, playbooks, and reusable tooling that increase the quality, consistency, and speed of delivery

 - Partner closely with the Project Management, Customer Success Management, Data/Integration, and Product teams to ensure a consistent customer experience, and channel field feedback into the product roadmap

 


REQUIREMENTS AND PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

 - 6 to 9 years of experience in software implementation, data migration, or technical consulting, ideally with enterprise or SaaS products

 - 5+ years of hands-on SQL scripting experience, including complex queries, data transformation, and reconciliation

 - 3+ years of Python, or similar, scripting experience for automation and data processing

 - Deep experience with database technologies and with ETL and data-migration concepts and tools, including schema design and performance considerations

 - Experience implementing AI-driven solutions for automation, workflow optimization, and data-driven insights, leveraging modern frameworks and AI models

 - Demonstrated ability to deliver complex implementations end to end and to mentor or provide technical guidance to less-experienced engineers

 - Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with a strong teamwork and customer-service mentality across executive and technical stakeholders

 - Strong attention to detail, with the proven ability to validate, reconcile, and sign off on data and configuration for accuracy

 - Ability to adapt to a rapidly changing product and respond strategically to evolving customer needs

 - Bachelor's degree in a technical, or related field

Job Summary

The Associate Implementation Engineer works directly with government customers to bring OpenGov cloud software to life, owning both the product configuration and the underlying data migration that make each implementation successful. This role confirms requirements, configures and tests the platform, migrates and validates customer data, and trains users, guiding customers through the full deployment journey from kickoff to go-live.

Acting as a trusted advisor with deep product knowledge and strong data and database expertise, the Associate Implementation Engineer understands each customer's goals, pain points, and workflows. This role blends hands-on technical delivery, including database schema management, ETL configuration, and scripting, with a consultative, customer-first approach, and partners across teams to ensure a smooth, high-quality implementation that maximizes the value customers realize from OpenGov.

Responsibilities

 - Deploy, configure, and test OpenGov cloud software to meet the documented implementation requirements of governments across the United States

 - Own customer data migration end to end, including database schema management, ETL tool configuration, and scripting as required, to ensure the product is populated with accurate, validated customer data

 - Confirm customer requirements across both configuration and data, and provide guidance, assistance, and support throughout the platform configuration and integration process

 - Ensure receipt of appropriate data from customers, map it to OpenGov requirements, and upload, transform, and manipulate it to generate the desired application behaviors

 - Build and execute test scenarios that validate the configuration and migrated data produce accurate, expected outcomes prior to go-live

 - Interact directly with government Finance staff, Budget Directors, IT personnel etc, and decision-makers, guiding them through the deployment and integration process

 - Identify customer pain points and partner with cross-functional teams to simplify, enhance, and automate existing processes that improve customer workflows

 - Troubleshoot configuration and data issues throughout the implementation and drive them to timely resolution

 - Work closely with the Project Management, Customer Success Management, Data/Integration, and Product teams to facilitate a consistent customer experience and ensure successful projects for customers

 - 0 to 1 year of SQL scripting experience

 - 0 to 1 year of Python, or similar, scripting experience

 - Strong Microsoft Excel and Word skills, including using functions/formulas to format data such as v-lookup, pivot tables, error-checking, and developing properly formatted reports

 - Experience with database technologies and with ETL or data-migration concepts and tools will be an advantage

 - Excellent interpersonal skills including verbal and written communication skills, teamwork, and customer service mentality

 - Ability to adapt to a rapidly changing product and respond strategically to customer needs

 - Strong attention to detail, with the ability to validate and reconcile data for accuracy

The ideal candidate is highly analytical, works independently, partners well across functions, and consistently meets deadlines while managing shifting priorities.

The ideal candidate is a proven people manager with a solid technical foundation in cloud-native infrastructure, including Kubernetes and containerized platforms, and a background in platform engineering or site reliability engineering. You should be comfortable managing technical teams, understanding operational challenges, facilitating cross-team discussions, and making sure priorities and expectations are clear.

This is a cross-functional role where you will partner closely with Customer Success, Product, Engineering, and Modeling teams to identify root causes, drive resolutions, and improve platform reliability.
The ideal candidate combines strong analytical skills, data modeling expertise, and a deep understanding of enterprise business processes. You will become a subject matter expert (SME) for customer implementations and platform modeling capabilities.

Join our team as an Independent Contractor for Project Morava.
 
 
Project Morava aims to help build more natural and intelligent voice AI systems by collecting high-quality speech data from native speakers.
 
 
In this project, participants contribute by reading and recording short, scripted prompts in Punjabi. These recordings are used to train and evaluate speech recognition models, enabling voice assistants and AI systems to better understand and respond to real-world users.
 
 
Project Benefits
- The entire task takes approximately 2 hours, including time to review the guidelines
- Work on your own schedule
- Participate from anywhere within India
- Record scripted prompts on your smartphone using the Appen Mobile app
 
 
Task Summary
You will use the Appen Mobile app on your smartphone to record 150 short, scripted voice prompts in Language. Each prompt is a brief spoken command — natural, everyday language. Simply read each prompt clearly and naturally, and you're done.
 
 
Requirements
- Must be a Native speaker of Punjabi
- Must be currently residing in India
- Female Participant
- Must be 18 years old or above
- Must have a smartphone compatible with the Appen Mobile app
 
 
Payment
Get paid for just 2 hours of work — completed entirely on your smartphone, on your own schedule. Payment is issued upon completion of a full session of 150 prompts. The quality bar is simple to hit: just follow the recording guidelines, speak clearly and naturally, and you're good to go. If assigned fewer than 150 prompts, payment is adjusted proportionally.
 
 
Please Note
This project follows a first-come, first-served approach and operates with demographic quotas to ensure fair and balanced representation across all participant groups. As a result, some individuals may not receive a task assignment if their group has already been filled.

Join us in shaping the future of voice AI. Your participation in Project Morava will directly help improve how technology understands and responds to real human speech.

Join Project Melora – Hindi Voice Recording ($2.40–$6)
Help build more natural voice AI by recording short, one-sided phone calls in Hindi. Imagine you're calling a bank, telco, or retailer for help, and speak naturally using made-up details. Each session takes only a few minutes.
Requirements
Native Hindi speaker, 18+
Can read and follow short instructions in Hindi
Own an iPhone 17, 17 Air, 17 Pro, or 17 Pro Max
Have a quiet indoor space to record (no TV, traffic, fans, or other voices)
Can complete 4–10 calls, each 1–2 minutes (5 minutes max)
Can spread calls out: no more than 3 per day, at least 3 hours apart, at different times of day across several days
Comfortable improvising a natural, unscripted call that follows a 6-step flow: greeting, ID verification, describing the issue, pausing for the agent's reply, resolution, and closing
Will use only fake names and account or order numbers (no real personal information)
Willing to be recorded, give recorded consent, sign an NDA, and follow project guidelines
How it works
Record solo calls on our secure platform. No second person is needed; pause where the agent would respond.
Submit basic metadata after each call.
Pay: $0.60 per QA-approved session
You need at least 4 approved sessions to be paid ($2.40), and you can do up to 10 ($6.00).
Sessions that fail QA don't count toward payment.
We recommend doing all 10 to get the full payout.
Why join? It's flexible and remote, you work on your own schedule, and pay is always above minimum wage in your market.

About the Role 
As an Applied Research Engineer, you’ll build practical AI research assets that support Frontier lab initiatives and customer engagements. This is an implementation-focused role for someone who enjoys turning research concepts into working systems. 
You’ll work with a high degree of autonomy, experimenting with new approaches and developing solutions that can be reused across customer opportunities. You’ll partner closely with the GenAI Research team and cross-functional stakeholders to bring technical ideas into practical applications. 
Your Impact 
Build reinforcement learning and agent environments for real customer and Frontier lab use cases, including task specifications, scoring, and evaluation.
Develop benchmarks and evaluation harnesses to measure model and data quality across areas such as accuracy, robustness, safety, latency, and cost.
Build LLM pipelines and agentic systems that support research, evaluation, and customer trials.
Run fine-tuning, adapter, and other model experiments to evaluate how data and methods influence model behavior.
Deploy local or self-hosted models for evaluation, inference, and automation workflows.
Document experiments, configurations, data, results, and known limitations so other engineers can reproduce and build on your work.
Partner with the GenAI Research team and cross-functional stakeholders to turn technical work into reusable assets for customer engagements. 
What You Bring

Ashoka is unleashing demand for empathy as a 21st century skill. Our Global Empathy Initiative has mobilized a powerful group of social entrepreneurs (Ashoka Fellows), schools (Ashoka Changemaker Schools), media thought leaders, and other partners to drive a fundamental shift in children’s education and coming of age.
 
We are looking for an extraordinary entrepreneur to lead the Empathy initiative for South Asia. This is a powerful opportunity for an imaginative, collaborative entrepreneur. If you are an accomplished leader (from any field) who has built or grown an organization from early stages to large size, has built teams, believes in the power of networks, and are looking for the next big challenge, come join us.

Ashoka’s vision is of an Everyone a Changemaker society, where every person — and young people in particular — have the confidence, ability, and support to be changemakers for the good of all. In a world defined by rapid change, interconnectedness and uncertainty, and where our social problems are deep and urgent, changemaking must become the new literacy. Such a shift is significant and will require a movement that fundamentally re-examines how young people grow up and learn — in and out of school — and how we see and support them today as change agents. It will require more than any specific curriculum or skill set, but rather a new mindset and new priorities.
 
The role of “Youth Years Leader” is focused on making sure that every young person self-actualizes as a changemaker. Ashoka is unleashing demand for these important 21st century skills of empathy, teamwork, new leadership, and changemaking in households and schools across the nation. To do this we have mobilized Ashoka Fellows across South Asia, and strategic partners across many sectors. The directive of this network is to create a fundamental shift where becoming a changemaker is as valuable as learning to read and write.
 
How? Our Theory of Change:  
 
Ashoka is not setting out to teach every child changemaking skills. Instead Ashoka is committed to act as a catalyst focused on creating a movement with partners such that demand for changemaking skills will grow rapidly.   Much like what we did with the field of social entrepreneurship, we are seeking to drive this mindset shift in society by helping people see differently. We intend to work with co-creators (Ashoka Fellows and other leaders) to influence key actors including, parents, schools, governments, media, and companies to see why changemaking skills are key for their children to succeed and contribute effectively in society. It will open opportunities to change how we parent, what we teach our children, what stories media puts out into the world, how we hire, organize, or report success.    
 
Metrics include – Do other key influencers now say changemaking skills are key? Are more parents prioritizing changemaking skills for their children? Are schools or governments now using pedagogy and curriculum to instill changemaking skills in teachers/children? Are companies looking to hire changemakers? Are big media platforms writing about changemaking?

Role Summary
Sophos is seeking an experienced and motivated Senior Penetration Testing Analyst 1 to join our Red Team. The Sophos Red Team is engaged by organizations worldwide to identify and exploit vulnerabilities within client environments, applying information security threat intelligence to uncover the same weaknesses real-world adversaries would target.
As a Senior Penetration Testing Analyst 1, you will act as the point of contact for testing readiness, coordinating tasks, timelines, and communication between business, client, and project teams. Responsible for escalating issues to management and taking ownership of new challenges to add value.  In addition to test readiness support, the position will focus on either application security (web application penetration testing, mobile, API testing) or network security (vulnerability assessments, external penetration tests, internal penetration tests, etc.), using both off-the-shelf and internally developed tools to execute manual testing for advanced attacks. Candidates are not expected to be experienced in both focus areas, although that would be a plus.
In this role, you will be responsible for test readiness activities to ensure engagements are ready to begin by troubleshooting client readiness problems, communicating with clients and tracking readiness status, and producing professional security assessment reports detailing vulnerability and exploit information for clients.  This position will lead client-facing calls throughout each engagement, from test readiness and troubleshooting, project kick-off through notification of high and critical findings to a close-out review of test findings, evidence, process steps to reproduce, and remediation recommendations.
The ideal candidate for this role will bring strong technical communication skills, sound analytical and problem-solving abilities, and a proactive approach to researching new threats, vulnerabilities, and exploits.
You will excel as both a self-directed individual contributor and as a member of a larger team, performing other essential duties as assigned.

We are seeking a highly skilled gNMI Engineer with strong expertise in SONiC (Software for Open Networking in the Cloud), network programmability, telemetry, and automation. The ideal candidate will be responsible for designing, developing, integrating, and maintaining gNMI-based management and telemetry solutions for SONiC-enabled network devices. The role requires deep understanding of YANG models, OpenConfig, gRPC/gNMI protocols, and modern datacentre networking technologies.
 
The engineer will work closely with SONiC developers, network architects, automation teams, and cloud infrastructure teams to build scalable network management and observability solutions.
 
What will you do ?
• Design and implement gNMI-based configuration and telemetry solutions for SONiC switches. Maintain gNMI clients, servers, and related services.
• Integrate SONiC management interfaces with OpenConfig and vendor-specific YANG models.

• Support integration of SONiC with data center orchestration platforms.

• Contribute to SONiC management framework enhancements.

• Contribute to SONiC Community.

• Experience with: NETCONF, gNOI, OpenTelemetry

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, excellent debugging and troubleshooting abilities.

Good to have

• Experience with hyperscale datacenter environments.

We are looking for a highly technical, hands-on Principal DV Engineer to anchor the verification of our next-generation, high-performance networking silicon. In this role, you will be the primary technical driver for complex IPs and critical sub-systems. You will balance advanced architectural environment creation with rigorous execution, leading by example on the engineering floor. This position is ideal for a veteran engineer who loves breaking complex designs, building elite UVM environments, and mentoring the next generation of verification talent.
Key Responsibilities
IP & Sub-system Leadership: Own the complete verification lifecycle for critical high-performance networking IPs and large-scale sub-systems.
UVM Environment Architecture: Architect, develop, and maintain advanced, scalable constrained-random verification environments from scratch using System Verilog and UVM.
Test Planning & Execution: Author comprehensive, bulletproof verification plans. Drive test case development, regressions, triage, and coverage closure (functional, code, and assertion-based metrics).
Advanced Debugging: Serve as the team's go-to expert for isolating and resolving the most complex, deep-seated hardware bugs.
Lead by Example: Actively participate in design and verification code reviews. Maintain high standards of code quality, reuse, and documentation within the execution team.
Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner closely with Design and Architecture teams to resolve ambiguities early in the design cycle and ensure high-quality delivery.

Experience: 15+ years of solid experience in ASIC/SoC Design Verification with a proven track record of successful tape-outs.
Domain Expertise: Extensive experience in the networking domain, verifying high-throughput, data-intensive designs.
Methodology Expert: Mastery of System Verilog and UVM. Must have a proven history of writing complex testbenches and VIP integrations from scratch.
Verification Scope: Proven experience leading verification at the IP and Sub-system level, with strong exposure to SoC integration.
Education: B Tech/M Tech in Electronics/Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
Preferred / Added Advantages
Hands-on experience with Formal Property Verification (FPV) to exhaustively verify block-level control logic.
Proficiency in Python or Perl for testbench automation and triage scripting.

Experience Level: 17+ Years (or 15+ with exceptional strategic track record)
Location: Bangalore, India (On-Site)
Position Type: Full-Time
About the Role
We are seeking a visionary Senior Principal DV Engineer to define the global verification strategy for our massive-scale networking SoCs. This is a high-impact, elite technical leadership role. You will be responsible for defining the overarching SoC verification methodology, driving cross-functional alignment from architecture to post-silicon, and pioneering next-generation verification technologies (such as Formal and Emulation). You will influence design architectures for verifiability and serve as a strategic technical advisor to executive leadership while steering the broader engineering organization.
Key Responsibilities
SoC Verification Strategy: Define, architect, and govern the overarching verification roadmap and methodology for full-scale, multi-million gate networking SoCs.
Methodology Innovation: Drive the adoption of advanced methodologies. Seamlessly integrate Formal Property Verification (FPV), hardware emulation, and advanced shift-left strategies into the standard SoC timeline.
High-Level Governance: Establish, track, and enforce rigorous quality metrics and sign-off criteria across the entire project lifecycle, ensuring zero-defect silicon.

jobs.role: Alpheratz Project - Burmese Translation Quality Reviewer
jobs.description:
We are looking for experienced language professionals to support an ongoing project focused on reviewing and refining Burmese customer service content. This role involves improving machine-translated materials to ensure accuracy, natural language, and alignment with project guidelines.
 
What you’ll do
Conduct second-pass quality reviews to ensure overall linguistic accuracy and consistency across batches.
Validate and calibrate severity assessments to maintain alignment with quality standards.
Identify systemic MT quality issues, including recurring error patterns, tone mismatches, and terminology inconsistencies.
Provide high-level qualitative feedback that directly contributes to final quality reporting and continuous improvement efforts.
 
Project details
Language:  Burmese
Hourly Rate: $10.63
Duration: 1-2 hours weekly

Welocalize, a Welo Global brand, serves localization teams through AI-enabled multilingual content solutions that enable enterprises to operate and scale globally. Build and maintain quality dashboards (throughput, accuracy, error mix, trend lines) and share concise summaries.

Manage access requests and permissions for QA tools and folders. 
Support vendor coordination (checklists, SLAs, documentation requests). 
Identify minor process gaps and suggest simple fixes (templates, checklists).
